reviewer_role: Independent task reviewer; implemented F1, did not implement or modify F2/F3
review_method: Read implementation, theorem derivation, existing logs and reported results; independently reconstruct interval/Krawczyk/domain arguments. No blanket campaign or existing test rerun. One targeted malformed-input countercheck built separately in reviews/.

accepted_guarantees.claim: Native outward original-residual certificates are mathematically valid under the documented binary64 environment for this bounded model.
accepted_guarantees.reason: Dyadic model coefficients are exact. Every non-dyadic Bernstein ratio and every 1/7,6/7,8/7 radius coefficient is computed by outward interval division. Each coefficient circuit encloses the exact rational Hermite candidate; Bernstein hulls enclose its entire slab. One-nextafter enclosures are valid for the stated RN binary64 operations with no FMA/FTZ/DAZ and no overflow.

accepted_guarantees.claim: Radius accumulation and same-branch continuation are valid across all slabs of the supported domain.
accepted_guarantees.reason: The fixed point map q_i=x_i-q_{i+1}^2/4 maps Q into itself with L=1/8. It gives 8/7 root residual sensitivity and parameter Lipschitz bound. Slow field has inward boundary signs on X and reduced contraction rate 6/7. Delta=Df+Dg/7, Ewhole=E+h*Delta, Eend=E/(1+6h/7)+h*Delta, Qwhole=(8/7)*(Ewhole+Dg) are valid upper bounds. Native arithmetic propagates Eend upward; exact zero initial root and global box uniqueness identify a single branch without chart switches.
evidence: native.cpp certificate and main slab loop

accepted_guarantees.claim: The method called krawczyk provides a valid post-Newton interval root enclosure for every uncached noninitial root solve in the recorded campaign.
accepted_guarantees.reason: J has entries J_jj=1 and J_{j-1,j}=q_j/2. Code uses M_ij=delta_ij-R_ij-R_{i,j-1}*Q_j/2, matching I-RJ. R is an arbitrary binary64 preconditioner, which is admissible. Outward g and J ranges and strict component radius tests imply K(B) strictly inside B. The same test implies ||I-RJ(q)||<1 and therefore R nonsingular. Cube membership in Q plus global contraction fixes branch identity.

accepted_guarantees.claim: The reported wall-clock comparison is fair within the stated first-passing-tested-grid tolerance contract.
accepted_guarantees.reason: Compiled, structured Newton and Newton-plus-Krawczyk all use the same model and final whole-path certificate; all first pass at N64 on the tested grid with almost identical root error bounds about 1.42e-9. Newton uses the same O(n) cyclic solve and warm-start/cache instead of an artificially expensive generic factorization. Krawczyk preconditioner and inclusion time remains included in integration and total time; shared certificate time is included. Offline source/object growth and compilation cost are separately reported. The documentation explicitly declines universal speedup and optimal-step claims.

accepted_guarantees.claim: Validation counts separate native certification from representative exact reference comparisons.
accepted_guarantees.reason: The native executable certifies every reported slab: 2160 distinct slabs, 15120 across 252 timed repeats of 36 configurations. The independent Fraction oracle is applied to 27 first/middle/last matched-run slabs and 135 bound comparisons only. Existing tests and documentation correctly state this representative coverage rather than implying all native slabs have been independently recomputed exactly.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The singleton interval constructor itself permits NaN or infinity; it is not a hardened general-purpose interval API. The supported scientific guarantee is explicitly for bounded finite model inputs, and the documented certificate paths do not rely on admitting nonfinite inputs.
nonblocking_findings.countercheck: A review-only probe confirms I(NaN) admits a singleton, but NaN in a slow endpoint, algebraic endpoint, Krawczyk parameter, or Krawczyk candidate is rejected by downstream interval validity checks (4/4). No false certificate was observed.
nonblocking_findings.action: Optional future hardening: reject nonfinite singleton inputs explicitly if exposing the interval type as a public general-purpose API. No change required for the present scoped campaign.

nonblocking_findings.finding: Timing records use seven in-process repeats in fixed configuration order; they are measurements, not a statistical speedup theorem. Certificate cost dominates and n16 compiled/Newton total ordering reverses. This is already correctly disclosed.
nonblocking_findings.action: Preserve the existing scope language and raw repeats; broader randomized and hardware campaigns are future work.

compiler_contract.rounding_assumptions: IEEE binary64 RN; no FTZ/DAZ, no fast-math, FMA disabled; finite bounded input domain

remaining_obligations: Do not generalize this finite structured cycle to arbitrary sparse algebraic systems or a generic compiler.
Do not claim all 2160 distinct native slabs have an exact-Fraction oracle comparison; exact independent coverage is 27.
No generic nonfinite-input interval-library guarantee, verified compiler guarantee, near-singular/stiff result, or universal timing advantage.
F1-dependent identity is the contraction-domain branch contract; this larger family does not test a nontrivial chart transition.
